terra.problem: The passage does not say that no guest has arrived when Wisdom finishes preparing the meal.
The passage does not say Wisdom is unable to sit still or that the whole neighborhood heard her. Marking the latter as a bet does not establish who heard her.
“Live” and “wander” are not close in sound.
The passage says the dead are there and Folly’s guests are in the depths of Sheol; it does not specifically describe suffering on the other road.
The passage says the person who corrects a mocker brings shame on himself. It does not say he receives no thank-you.
The verse says the wise man will love the person who rebukes him, not that he thanks him.
The verse says the mocker will hate the person who rebukes him, not that he hates the rebuke.
“Before the years of learning pile up” adds a timeline the verse does not give.
The explanation repeats the answer in several generic ways without much of Papa Dorin’s voice.
The verse does not say what resting will or will not do about the consequences.
The verse does not say whether anyone can wait out the consequences.
The opening words match, but saying Folly sounds just like the other invitation overstates the match.
The same words do not establish whether Folly speaks more softly than Wisdom.
Folly calls bread eaten in secret tasty, but the text does not say it is tasty because it is eaten in secret.
Bread eaten in secret is not necessarily the opposite of bread shared with friends; it could be both.
Folly does not make her invitation sound like a royal feast. The passage says nothing about royalty in her pitch.
The passage does not say there is no treasure in Folly’s house.
The passage says they do not know what is there, not that they cannot see inside.
